rule: P2a-1: highest observed value reported by the source series, rounded up to one significant digit (Protocol Sec. 2 Tier 2, Clause 2)
source_citation: Walshe JM. The pattern of urinary copper excretion and its response to treatment in patients with Wilson's disease. QJM 2011;104(9):775-778. doi:10.1093/qjmed/hcr073. FULL TEXT OBTAINED 2026-08-30 (institutional OUP subscription); the Discussion reports the observed minimum and maximum for all three groups of the 192 Wilson's disease patients: pre-symptomatic 11-550, hepatic 61-3080, neurological 61-782 ug/24h. The adopted value is the largest of the three group maxima (hepatic group, n=37, 3080 ug/24h). The patient with 3080 was in a massive haemolytic crisis and the source states that such a single figure 'will skew the statistics'; that is a caution about the group MEAN, not a denial of eligibility as an attainable upper limit, so the case is NOT excluded (Clause 1: a bound is the highest attainable measured value, not a representative distribution). This supersedes the earlier P2a-3 derivation from the hepatic group mean 465.75 ug/24h, which was adopted only because the abstract alone was available and reported no range. The EASL penicillamine-challenge threshold had been replaced earlier because it is a post-challenge value (Clause 0). Timing evidence: Dickson ER et al. Hepatology 1989;10(1):1-7 (trial data collected at entry; Table 1 urine copper median 73 matches survival::pbc)
